label: insert-after pilot: Explain -> Reveal -> Manipulate -> Generalize on the steppedReveal wall (rev: graded act = locate the critical point; endpoint insight at success — the first draft's highFeedback was DEAD with targetX at the slider max, caught by the solvability gate)

step.body: The reveal's claim, live. Find the flat tangent yourself — then look at where the curve is actually tallest.

predict.prompt: This window shows f(x) = x³ on [−4, 4]. Somewhere the tangent goes flat. Will that flat point be the tallest point of the window?

options.label: No — the flat point isn't the top here
x³ never has a flat tangent

predict.reveal: Drag and watch the f′ pane: it touches zero at x = 0 while the curve climbs straight past — the tallest point is the right edge, where f′ = 48.

widget.prompt: Drag the point until the tangent is FLAT — drive f′ to zero — and watch what the curve does there.
widget.successFeedback: f′ = 0 at x = 0 — and yet the curve climbs straight past it. Flat found you a candidate, not the champion: the tallest point on this window is the right edge, where f′ = 48. That endpoint is exactly what the theorem makes you check.
widget.lowFeedback: Not flat yet — the f′ pane is still above zero here, and the curve is still climbing. Keep moving right toward where f′ dips to zero.
widget.highFeedback: You passed it — f′ is positive again and climbing. Back up to where the lower pane touches zero.

refusals.title: The Definite Integral (running backwards flips the sign)
refusals.why: The authored steppedReveal teaches ORIENTATION: integrating from b to a makes every dx negative, so the sum flips sign. riemannSum is the only area engine, and it has no notion of traversal direction — its spec is a, b, tolerance, nStart, ruleStart (schema.ts:3153-3163) and its grader compares riemannEstimate(fn, a, b, n, rule) against exactArea(fn, a, b) (evaluate.ts:1488-1494), both of which presume a forward interval. An inserted lab could show area accumulating, but never the dx < 0 mechanism the reveal actually teaches — the models gate of the three-gate fit test fails.

refusals.title: Concavity (curve-analysis)
refusals.why: The reveal's subject is f″ and inflection. derivativeTrace draws exactly two panes, f and f′ (widgets.tsx:4081-4086, traced via traceSlopeAt), with fn limited to square|cubic|abs (schema.ts:3136) and no second-derivative representation. A lab that cannot SHOW concavity changing cannot let the learner manipulate it — represents gate fails. Needs either an f″ mode on derivativeTrace or a dedicated engine; recorded as an engine gap, not patched around.
